claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model should be certified for launch on a narrow conditional basis: aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, rollout starts at 7% with rollback and monitoring, and certification is supportable only if the model card explicitly discloses the clinical coding assistant observation-status limitation because that exposed segment remains below target and no approved risk acceptance covers it.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the certification satisfies the policy threshold at launch.
Treat the clinical coding assistant weakness as material because the evidence says the segment is below target and remains exposed in the initial cohort.

Under the policy, rollout controls and monitoring mitigate deployment risk but do not remove disclosure duties unless the affected use case is excluded or approved risk acceptance covers the exposure.
A conditional rationale can be logically derived from admissible evidence, but a locked certify_model decision requires evidence that the condition has actually been satisfied.
evidence_requests: Provide the final launch model card or equivalent disclosure artifact showing the observation-status limitation is explicitly disclosed for the clinical coding assistant use case.
Provide approval or release-check evidence showing that disclosure will be in place before launch.
If certification is to rely on risk acceptance instead of disclosure, provide an approved risk-acceptance document that specifically addresses the exposed clinical coding assistant segment.
specific_concerns: The admissible evidence shows a material weakness remains in an exposed launch segment.
The policy text says rollout controls, rollback, dashboards, and small initial percentages do not remove disclosure duties when the affected use case remains exposed.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has actually been prepared, approved, or will be present at launch.
The risk-acceptance document is only a draft, has no approver, and does not cover the exposed clinical coding assistant segment.
The Actor's locked recommendation of certify_model is stronger than the evidence currently supports because the required disclosure predicate is still unmet in the record.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that certification is presently compliant without first showing the required launch disclosure exists.
Any implication that rollback, monitoring, or a 7% rollout can substitute for disclosure under the stated policy.
Any implication that an approved risk acceptance already covers the clinical coding assistant exposure.
